results.quote: Theorem 1.4 (Informal Theorem 4.1). Let \(\epsilon>0\). Any 3SUM instance (A,B,C) where one of the sets has rank at most \(O(n^{1-\epsilon})\) can be solved in time \(O(n^{2-\epsilon'})\) for some \(\epsilon'>0\).

Theorem 1.6 (Small-Universe Reduction). Let \(\gamma\in[0,1]\). Min-Plus Convolution for length-n input sequences over a universe of size \(u=n^\gamma\) cannot be solved in time \(O(n^{1+\gamma-\epsilon})\) (for any constant \(\epsilon>0\)), unless the Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis fails.

results.bound: Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis \iff Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis (under Hypothesis 1.7)
results.quote: Theorem 1.8 (Large-Universe Reduction). Under Hypothesis 1.7, the Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis and the Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis are equivalent.
Theorem 1.9 (Min-Max Convolution). Min-Max Convolution cannot be solved in time \(O(n^{3/2-\epsilon})\) (for any constant \(\epsilon>0\)), unless the Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis fails.

Theorem 1.10 (Min-Equality Convolution). Min-Equality Convolution cannot be solved in time \(O(n^{3/2-\epsilon})\) (for any constant \(\epsilon>0\)), unless the Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis fails.

Theorem 1.11 (Bounded Monotone Min-Plus Convolution). Min-Plus Convolution between an arbitrary sequence and a monotone sequence bounded by [_n_] cannot be solved in time \(O(n^{3/2-\epsilon})\) (for any constant \(\epsilon>0\)), unless the Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis fails.

Theorem 1.12 (Min-Witness Convolution). Min-Witness Convolution cannot be solved in time \(O(n^{4/3-\epsilon})\) (for any constant \(\epsilon>0\)), unless the Strong Min-Plus Convolution Hypothesis fails.
